newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIAN WOOL EXPECTED TO STABILISE THIS WEEK.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIAN WOOL EXPECTED TO STABILISE THIS WEEK.

text.p: Weakness evident in last week's Australian wool market is not expected to continue this week and prices are expected to stabilise, Wesfarmers Dalgety Ltd said.
The sharp downturn in the market last week was greater than many expected, the broker said its its weekly market preview.

"However, the final day of sales yielded a distinct positive change in market sentiment and confidence, acting to stabilise prices as the sales closed," it said. This provided a good indicator of the coming week's activity, it said.

Lower prices, China's increased global wool import quota and the Australian dollar's lowest point in 18 months at 73.30 U.S. cents last Wednesday were expected to support market activity this week, Wesfarmers Dalgety said.

However, the large quantities offer -- with an extra 13,000 bales on the market because of early shearings in response to quickly drying conditions in many areas -- continued to overhang the market and this could restrict any upturn, the broker said.
About 100,151 bales are rostered for sale this week.
The eastern market indicator fell 22 cents to 696 cents/kg clean last week.
